claims.text: Adding approximately 2 at.% Ti shifts the phase equilibrium of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni toward a single disordered FCC or BCC solid solution.
The Ti addition suppresses formation of brittle, coarse intermetallic compounds.
The altered phase balance is responsible for maintaining high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation resistance, and cryogenic toughness simultaneously.
The baseline Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy typically contains a mixture of disordered solid solution and minor intermetallic phases.
The mixed phases in the baseline alloy limit its overall balance of performance.
A predominantly disordered FCC or BCC solid solution with reduced intermetallic formation mediates improved multi-temperature mechanical properties.
Ti creates local lattice strain in the alloy.
Ti changes the atomic-size mismatch in the alloy.
Ti-induced lattice strain and atomic-size mismatch suppress nucleation and growth of brittle intermetallic phases.
Ti-induced lattice strain and atomic-size mismatch stabilize the disordered phase.
The proposed phase stabilization preserves high-temperature strength.
The proposed phase stabilization improves resistance to environmental degradation.
The proposed phase stabilization improves resistance to radiation-induced defects.
The proposed phase stabilization maintains toughness at cryogenic temperatures.
The Ti-modified alloy will contain more than 80% stable disordered phase, compared with less than 70% in the baseline.
The Ti-modified alloy will show a statistically significant improvement in high-temperature strength relative to the baseline.
The Ti-modified alloy will show a statistically significant improvement in radiation tolerance relative to the baseline.
The Ti-modified alloy will show a statistically significant improvement in environmental resistance relative to the baseline.
The Ti-modified alloy will show a statistically significant improvement in cryogenic toughness relative to the baseline.
